title: 3D Imaging of Soft-Tissue Samples using an X-ray Specific Staining Method and Nanoscopic Computed Tomography
protocol: Fill a 50-mL centrifuge tube with a fixative solution containing 9.5 mL of 4% (v/v) formaldehyde solution and 0.5 mL of glacial acetic acid.
Prepare a fresh FA solution from a 37% acid free FA stabilized with approximately 10% methanol.
Dilute the FA solution further with Dulbecco’s phosphate buffered saline (DPBS) without calcium and magnesium.
Add freshly removed soft-tissue sample to a 50-mL centrifuge tube.
Refrigerate the 50-mL centrifuge tube for 24-72 hours.
Wash the soft-tissue sample with DPBS solution for 1 hour.
Place the soft-tissue in 2 mL of eosin Y-staining solution and incubate the sample for 24 h on a horizontal shaking plate at approximately 60 rpm.
Remove excess staining agent with cellulose tissue paper.
Place the soft-tissue sample in a conical sample container above an ethanol vapor phase for storage.
Add a few drops of 70% ethanol to the bottom of the conical sample container.
Mount the soft-tissue sample onto an appropriate sample holder.
Ensure the sample is tightly secured on the sample holder to prevent movement during X-ray CT measurements.
Prepare a sample holder with two centrifuge tubes, cutting off the bottom of one tube for mouse kidney samples.
Glue the two centrifuge tubes together using two-component adhesive and wait for it to harden.
Transfer the mouse kidney into the intact centrifuge tube containing a few drops of 70% ethanol.
Maintain soft-tissue sample over an ethanol vapor phase during X-ray CT measurements to keep it moist.
Prevent the soft-tissue sample from coming into direct contact with solvent to avoid accumulation around the sample.
Place a cellulose paper moistened with 70% (v/v) ethanol in the sample holder if necessary.
Choose acquisition parameters for best image quality.
Acquire the scan at a peak voltage of 50 kV, a current of 3.5 W using 1601 projections equally distributed over 360°.
Select the 0.39x camera objective to cover the whole sample within the field of view (FOV).
Use an effective pixel size of 12 µm and an exposure time of 2 s per projection for a good signal-to-noise ratio.
Identify the ROI for the high-resolution CT scan using microCT data from the overview scan.
Choose the 4x camera objective resulting in an effective pixel size of 3.3 µm for high-resolution CT data acquisition.
Use an exposure time of 15 s per projection for high-resolution CT scans.
Reconstruct the X-ray CT data with integrated software.
Generate volume renderings using visualization software.
Cut soft tissue into pieces approximately 0.5 mm edge length using a scalpel and stereomicroscope.
Dehydrate samples in ethanol concentrations of 50%, 60%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, and 100% (all v/v) balanced with distilled water, each for 1 hour.
Keep small tissue pieces in 100% ethanol overnight.
Critical point dry the small tissue pieces.
Prefill the vacuum chamber with 100% ethanol.
Transfer small tissue pieces into a micro-porous capsule and place it in the vacuum chamber of the CPD.
Close the system.
Cool the chamber to 6-8°C and fill up with liquid CO2.
Stir while waiting for proper mixing of ethanol and CO2 for 3 minutes.
Carefully drain the chamber.
Ensure the sample holder is still covered with solvent.
Repeat this step ten times to allow complete replacement of ethanol with CO2 within the sample.
Heat the machine to the critical point of CO2 (31 °C and 73.8 bar).
Release gaseous CO2 very slowly over 30 minutes.
Ensure the temperature does not drop below the critical point of CO2 during release.
Open the CPD machine only when all pressure has been released from the system.
Remove the CPD tissue pieces quickly and place them in a new Petri dish stored in a desiccator.
Mount the CPD tissue pieces to an appropriate sample holder.
Glue the tissue pieces with superglue to the sample holder if necessary.
Ensure a tight fit of the sample on the sample holder to prevent movement during CT measurements.
Choose acquisition parameters for best image quality after careful alignment of the sample.
Apply Paganin’s phase-retrieval algorithm to the sharpened images.
Set parameters of the algorithm to optimize image quality.
Reconstruct the preprocessed projections using a filtered backprojection algorithm.
